B: σ1 receptor activation reduces ER stress and enhances autophagy in Mtb-infected macrophages
C: Enhanced intracellular killing of drug-resistant Mtb and reduced granuloma necrosis
statement: Fluvoxamine, via σ1R agonism, can reinvigorate autophagy in MDR-TB-infected macrophages, leading to bacterial clearance.

B: Inhibition of ALDH leads to accumulation of toxic aldehydes and copper-dependent Fenton reaction in Mtb
C: Bactericidal activity against replicating and non-replicating drug-resistant Mtb
statement: Repurposed disulfiram, a safe, copper-chelating alcohol-aversion drug, kills drug-resistant Mtb by exacerbating oxidative stress through aldehyde accumulation and copper-mediated ROS generation.

B: AMPK activation inhibits mTORC1 and promotes mitochondrial ROS in Mtb-infected macrophages
C: Suppression of intracellular growth of drug-resistant Mtb and reduced inflammation
statement: Metformin, a diabetes drug, enhances host-mediated killing of drug-resistant Mtb by inducing mitochondrial ROS via AMPK-mTORC1 axis in macrophages.

B: Inhibition of Rac1 blocks Mtb-induced macropinocytosis and actin tail-driven intercellular spread
C: Reduced dissemination of drug-resistant Mtb and lower burden in extrapulmonary sites
statement: Ketorolac, an NSAID, can block cell-to-cell spread of drug-resistant Mtb by inhibiting the host Rac1-dependent actin reorganization required for macropinocytosis-mediated bacterial transfer.

B: c-KIT inhibition depletes infected permissive monocytes and prevents myeloid progenitor expansion in bone marrow
C: Decreased recruitment of M.tb-permissive monocyte subsets to granulomas, enhancing bacterial control
statement: Imatinib, a tyrosine kinase inhibitor, can limit mycobacterial dissemination by blocking c-KIT-driven expansion of a permissive monocyte reservoir that drug-resistant Mtb exploits.

B: UDCA inhibits FXR and modulates autophagy in macrophages exposed to cholesterol-rich environments
C: Enhanced phagolysosomal fusion and killing of cholesterol-accumulating drug-resistant Mtb in foamy macrophages
statement: The bile acid UDCA, by antagonizing FXR, can restore cholesterol-driven autophagic defects, enabling foamy macrophages to clear drug-resistant Mtb that persist in cholesterol-rich granulomas.

B: Blockade of macrophage β2-adrenergic receptors reduces catecholamine-enhanced growth of Mtb via iron uptake
C: Reduced bacterial burden in iron-rich caseous granulomas of drug-resistant TB
statement: Propranolol can limit drug-resistant Mtb growth by inhibiting catecholamine-induced iron acquisition systems, essentially starving Mtb in granulomas.

B: mTOR-independent autophagy induction via inositol depletion and AMPK activation
C: Clearance of intracellular rifampicin-resistant Mtb through enhanced autophagic degradation
statement: Carbamazepine, an anticonvulsant, induces robust autophagy through inositol starvation and AMPK, killing drug-resistant intracellular Mtb.

B: Inhibition of Mtb thioredoxin reductase (TrxR) causing thiol-redox imbalance and accumulation of oxidized intermediates
C: Bactericidal effect against drug-resistant Mtb, including persisters under hypoxia
statement: Auranofin, an antirheumatic gold compound, kills drug-resistant Mtb by targeting thioredoxin reductase, disrupting the essential thiol-redox homeostasis needed for surviving oxidative stress.

B: cGMP-dependent protein kinase G (PKG) activation in macrophages enhances lysosomal trafficking and fusion
C: Increased degradation of phagocytosed drug-resistant Mtb within acidified phagolysosomes
statement: Sildenafil, by elevating cGMP, can potentiate bactericidal activity of macrophages against drug-resistant Mtb through PKG-mediated phagosome maturation.

B: Low-dose naltrexone (LDN) blocks TLR4, reducing necrotic and excessive inflammatory signaling in granulomas
C: Better containment of drug-resistant Mtb with less tissue destruction and cavity formation
statement: Low-dose naltrexone can limit immunopathology in MDR-TB granulomas by antagonizing TLR4-driven necrosis, thereby reducing bacterial dissemination and preserving lung function.

B: PPARα activation shifts macrophage metabolism from glycolysis to fatty acid oxidation, reducing availability of lactate and itaconate
C: Reduced intracellular growth of drug-resistant Mtb that relies on host glycolytic intermediates and lactate
statement: Fenofibrate, a lipid-lowering drug, can starve intracellular drug-resistant Mtb by metabolic reprogramming of macrophages away from glycolysis towards FAO.

B: Inhibition of host carbonic anhydrases acidifies the granuloma microenvironment and compromises Mtb pH homeostasis
C: Growth inhibition of extracellular drug-resistant Mtb in caseous lesions
statement: Acetazolamide, a diuretic, can acidify the granuloma microenvironment and directly impede drug-resistant Mtb by disrupting its ability to maintain intracellular pH in the acidic caseum.

B: Lowering cholesterol in phagosomal membranes enhances phagolysosome maturation and reduces Mtb access to cholesterol
C: Increased killing of intracellular MDR-TB and reduced granuloma cholesterol content
statement: Simvastatin, a statin, can improve macrophage killing of drug-resistant Mtb by reducing membrane cholesterol and promoting phagosome maturation.

B: Inhibition of macrophage efflux pumps increases intracellular retention of anti-TB drugs and host antimicrobial peptides
C: Potentiation of standard drugs against drug-resistant Mtb by achieving higher intracellular concentrations
statement: Verapamil can overcome drug-resistant Mtb tolerance by inhibiting macrophage drug efflux transporters that limit intraphagosomal antibiotic concentrations, acting as an adjuvant.
